desks.Dividends: MSFT goes ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the raised quarterly rate declared Sep 15 (+7.7%, its 24th consecutive annual increase) — the only declared watchlist ex-date in the next four weeks. AAPL's November dividend is still undeclared; the early-to-mid-November projection (TalkMarkets lists Nov 10) at the unchanged $0.27 rests on pattern only, and the declaration expected alongside Nov 2 earnings is what would turn it into fact. SPY, QQQ, and NVDA next go ex in December, outside the window; TSLA pays no dividend. No cuts or specials announced.
desks.Earnings: MSFT Wed Oct 28 after close is the week's binary event, on FOMC day, with its implied move unresolved at 5.3% on the fresher own calculation against 7.6% on a sourced Oct 18 read — no single figure is asserted until Monday's chain is recomputed. AAPL Mon Nov 2 after close follows with a convergent implied move of ~4.8-5.0%. Nasdaq consensus is $4.71 for MSFT and $2.00 for AAPL. Historical average earnings-day moves for both names are UNVERIFIED. TSLA already reported Oct 21 and is priced in; NVDA's date is unconfirmed, with trackers listing Nov 17, 18, and 25, so the Nov 18 date in the IV inputs file is an estimate only.
desks.Futures: Crude is pricing a geopolitical risk premium, not a confirmed supply shortfall: Brent $116.72 and WTI $103.27 at Friday's close, while the physical-flow picture is itself contested (above 24M barrels per day through Hormuz and alternative routes in the week through Oct 18, against ~13 tankers per day in today's read). The EIA print argues against chasing the crude headline: crude drew 3.1M barrels and gasoline 3.0M, but distillates built 1.7M and Cushing built 0.9M. Natural gas storage rose 77 Bcf to 3,644 Bcf, near normal nationally with a South Central deficit. Grains run the other way: October WASDE raised corn to a near-record crop and pushed futures down ~5%. Next catalysts: EIA Wed Oct 28, EIA gas Thu Oct 29, WASDE Tue Nov 10.
desks.Parity: No new put-call or box parity violation found, and deterministic parity stands as the pricing constraint. The one methodology item, carried from yesterday: S&P Dow Jones Indices revises its growth/value style scoring — momentum drops from growth scoring, value scoring moves to an intangibles-adjusted book-to-price with earnings- and cash-flow-to-price blends — before market open Dec 21, 2026, with pro-forma files due Dec 4. That is a style-subindex reclassification, not a headline index membership change, so the direct effect on SPY/QQQ tracking is limited; the flow to watch is style-index fund rebalancing around Dec 21. A secondhand estimate of $375B or more in passive funds tied to the affected gauges is UNVERIFIED against a primary source.
desks.Premium: Term structure slopes up everywhere because the earnings humps sit in the Nov 20 expiry, which contains MSFT (Oct 28), AAPL (Nov 2), and NVDA (Nov 18 estimated) — elevated back-month implied volatility for those names is expected event pricing, not rich premium. MSFT: 34.5% in Nov 20 against 22.7% front on today's live pull. No clean IV-versus-realized verdict for QQQ, AAPL, or NVDA: their realized windows are window-contingent (32.0%, 36.4%, and 31.0% single-day shares), with NVDA newly over the line. SPY, MSFT, and TSLA windows rolled clean. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names; no free IV-history source was available. Today's live levels run systematically above yesterday's live levels for the same expiry and closes, so cross-day level comparisons are unreliable; Friday-close marks are not executable quotes.
desks.Quant lab: Four candidates scored and appended to the ledger (#148-151): two ARCHIVE, two WATCH. The WATCH items are Yajrzyna/spy-atm-iv-forecasting (#150, score 46: SPY ATM IV forecasting where simple OLS beat LSTM out of sample, but blocked on licensed OptionsDX data not included in the repo) and h-a-forster/surfbench (#151, score 54: an arbitrage-free IV surface-fit benchmark whose held-out, next-snapshot, and arbitrage-violation scorecard ports directly to the desk's SPY surface-fit choice). headline: Daily research brief — Sunday, October 25

items.detail: Microsoft reports Wed Oct 28 after close, the same day as the FOMC decision, so the Oct 28-30 move cannot be attributed to earnings alone. The implied move is unresolved: the fresher own calculation from the Oct 23 chain puts the Oct 30 straddle at ~5.3% (mid $27.68 against $524.51), while a sourced Oct 18 read puts it at ~7.6% — different chain dates and possibly different strike and expiry selection, and neither figure is asserted as the single number until Monday's live chain is recomputed. Apple follows Mon Nov 2 after close with a convergent implied move of ~4.8-5.0%, consistent with yesterday's own ~4.9% recomputation. Nasdaq consensus is EPS $4.71 for MSFT (14 estimates, against $4.13 last year) and $2.00 for AAPL (8 estimates, against $1.85). Historical average earnings-day moves for both names are UNVERIFIED, and premium into either binary is event premium, not mispricing on its own.
items.title: MSFT Oct 28 lands on FOMC day; its implied move is unresolved

items.detail: Brent settled Fri Oct 23 at $116.72, up 3.14% on the day and its highest close since Apr 29, with WTI at $103.27 (+3.8%), a $13.45 spread, in steep backwardation. The price rise alongside disputed flow readings points to a fear and insurance premium — shipping risk and record Persian Gulf freight rates — rather than barrels already lost, and the premium can unwind as fast as it built. The two flow readings cannot both describe the same measure: yesterday's package reported Middle East crude exports through Hormuz and alternative routes above 24M barrels per day in the week through Oct 18, while today's desk reports Hormuz effectively closed to normal traffic at ~13 tankers per day against ~100 pre-crisis. Neither flow figure should be cited as settled until a primary Kpler/OPIS read reconciles them. The EIA print tempers the bull case further: crude drew 3.1M barrels and gasoline 3.0M, but distillates built 1.7M and Cushing built 0.9M.
items.title: Crude at $116 prices war premium, and the flow evidence is contested

The term structure slopes up everywhere because the earnings humps sit in the Nov 20 expiry, which contains MSFT (Oct 28), AAPL (Nov 2), and NVDA (Nov 18 estimated, date unconfirmed): MSFT implied volatility is 34.5% in Nov 20 against 22.7% in the front weekly on today's live pull, so the event premium lives in the back expiry, not the front week. items.detail: The latest FRED daily prints are dated Thu Oct 22 — Friday data had not landed at pull time, so these repeat yesterday's levels, a data lag rather than a new observation. The 2-year fell 16 basis points to 4.65% and the 10-year fell 17 to 4.96% on Oct 22, with the 2s10s spread at 31 basis points, still upward-sloping but 16 basis points flatter than 60 days ago. The fed funds effective rate is 3.88% and SOFR prints 3.90%, a 2-basis-point spread that signals no funding stress. One day of relief does not reverse a 60-day rise of 30 to 48 basis points: absolute levels near 5% on the 10-year remain a discount-rate headwind for long-duration names. The event stack is the Oct 28 FOMC decision, with core PCE landing Oct 29, after the decision.
